[[184 BBY]]''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' establishes that Taibik Kajok is fifty-two [[Standard year|years]] old during the main events of ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which take place in [[132 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:TheAcolyteDate|here]]. Therefore, he must have been [[Reproduction|born]] around [[184 BBY]]. ''The Acolyte: The Visual Guide'' also establishes [[Wiltoo Kajok]] was forty-nine years old during the events of ''The Acolyte'', meaning he was born around [[181 BBY]]. |death= |species=[[Huwawan]] |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.78 [[meter]]s (5 [[Foot|ft]] 10 in) |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes= |skin=[[Color|Tan]] |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners= |siblings=[[Wiltoo Kajok]] |children= |affiliation= |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|What did they say?''"
"''Seems an umbramoth colony hatched last night and wreaked havoc on a local settlement.|Vernestra Rwoh and Mog Adana, discussing information they learned from Taibik and Wiltoo Kajok|{{Acolyte|Teach / Corrupt}}}} '''Taibik Kajok''' was a [[Huwawan]] [[Gender|male]] from the [[planet]] [[Khofar]] who was [[Reproduction|born]] around [[184 BBY]]. When they were younger, Taibik and his younger brother [[Wiltoo Kajok]] worked as guides leading tourists through Khofar's [[forest]]s. When they became older, the two brothers instead remained at their tent near the basic [[spaceport]] they maintained, where they bartered and sold safety tips, [[map]] programs, and survival gear. In [[132 BBY]], Taibik used a [[fuel]] pump while a [[Khofar Jedi task force|Jedi task force]] [[Mission to Khofar|visited]] the spaceport. The next [[Local day|morning]], Taibik and Wiltoo played a game of [[dejarik]] together. Later that day, they spoke with another [[Jedi]] team who had come to investigate the [[death]]s of the first team, informing them that an [[umbramoth]] colony had hatched the previous night. ==Biography== Taibik Kajok was a [[Huwawan]] [[Gender|male]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Khofar]] who was [[Reproduction|born]] around [[184 BBY]]. He was the older brother of [[Wiltoo Kajok]], who was born around [[181 BBY]]. The brothers maintained a [[spaceport]] that consisted only of the most basic amenities for travelers, where they bartered and sold safety tips, [[map]] programs, and survival gear. When they were younger, the brothers worked as guides who led tourists along the few trails in Khofar's [[forest]]s. During Taibik's final time accompanying an expedition, his face was scratched by an [[umbramoth]]. When Taibik and Wiltoo became older, they instead stayed at a dockside tent and wished explorers luck. [[File:KajokBrothersTent-TeachCorrupt.png|thumb|right|300px|Taibik and Wiltoo speak to the second Jedi team at their tent.]] In [[132 BBY]],{{TheAcolyteDate}} a [[Khofar Jedi task force|Jedi task force]] arrived on Khofar to [[Mission to Khofar|extract]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Kelnacca]] from his post there and landed at the brothers' spaceport. While [[Padawan]] [[Jecki Lon]] questioned Wiltoo using a [[translatacomp]], Taibik removed a [[Color|blue]] tube from{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}} a dilapidated [[fuel]] pump and connected it to another device. When Wiltoo rose indignantly,{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}} {{AD|Disney+}} Taibik briefly stepped away from the pump and gestured toward another individual crouched near it, then returned the tube to the fuel pump. The [[Jedi]] then headed into the forest to search for Kelnacca, where most of them were [[Death|killed]] by the [[Sith]] known as [[the Stranger]]. The next morning, Taibik and Wiltoo played a low-tech, high-stakes version of the game [[dejarik]] on a rustic board and ignored{{Acolyte|Night}} {{AD|Disney+}} the surviving members of the Jedi team walking past them.{{Acolyte|Night}} Although the brothers pooled their [[Currency|money]], their [[Gambling|wagering]] grew heated, and Wiltoo knocked several pieces off the board. Jedi Master [[Vernestra Rwoh]] later arrived at the spaceport with another team to investigate the Jedi's deaths. Taibik and Wiltoo spoke to the team in an obscure variant of [[Huwawi]] and informed them that an Umbramoth colony had hatched the previous night. As Padawan{{Databank|mog-adana|Mog Adana}} [[Mog Adana]] reported what they had learned to Rwoh, suggesting it could have been the cause of the deaths, the brothers continued speaking with another Jedi. The team then left to investigate the location where the Jedi had died. ==Personality and traits== Taibik Kajok had tan skin, brown [[hair]], and dark [[eye]]s, and his face bore a scratch from an umbramoth. He stood 1.78 [[meter]]s (5 [[Foot|feet]], 10 inches) tall. By 132 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], when he was fifty-two standard years old, he had creaking [[bone]]s and a sore back, and had had his fill of thrill-seekers who wandered off-trail. As a result, Taibik chose to stay by his dockside tent with his brother. He was less ambitious then Wiltoo, who envisioned turning their land into more than a barren field. Taibik and Wiltoo filled their time by playing dejarik, and although they pooled their money, their betting grew heated. He prided himself on having the sharpest business acumen. ==Skills and abilities== Kajok spoke an obscure variant of Huwawi that was difficult for Jedi translatacomps to analyze. ==Equipment== Kajok wore black [[boot]]s, black [[Clothing|pants]], and a brown shirt, over which he wore rough fiber made from the stems of the Khofari [[iotii plant]]. He also wore a [[belt]] to which he strapped a woven [[hat]] made from [[raffu plant]] leaves and self-launching emergency [[flare]] canisters on his chest, and another piece of equipment with silver cylinders on his right arm. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:TaibikConcept-ArtofAcolyte.png|thumb|right|200px|Concept art by Ivan Manzella]] Taibik Kajok first appeared, albeit unidentified, in "[[Day (episode)|Day]]," the fourth episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', which aired on [[June 18]], [[2024]].{{SW|url=series/the-acolyte/season-1-episode-4-day-episode-guide|text="Day" Episode Guide | The Acolyte}} He was identified in [[Pablo Hidalgo]]'s [[2025]] reference book, ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]''. The scenes at the Khofar landing site{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-1-madeira|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 1: Madeira|archivedate=20241204220147}} including Kajok were shot at the [[Wikipedia:Portugal|Portuguese]] island [[Wikipedia:Madeira Island|Madeira]]. Concept art of Taibik was created by [[Ivan Manzella]]. Taibik and Wiltoo were originally designed to be patrons of the [[Lomi Usqi Noodle Shop]] during the opening sequence of the first episode of ''The Acolyte'', "[[Lost / Found]],"''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' which aired on [[June 3]], 2024.{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-teaser-poster|text=''The Acolyte'' Teaser Poster, Premiere Date Revealed}} However, showrunner [[Leslye Headland]] liked the look of the brothers so much that they were moved to the landing site, a location with more sun. The [[2026]]{{Abrams|url=product/art-of-star-wars-the-acolyte_9781419777349|text=The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte}} reference book ''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'', written by [[Kristin Baver]], describes Taibik and Wiltoo as [[twin]]s, although ''Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide'' had previously established the brothers to be different ages. ===Concept art gallery=== {{Gallery |source=''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' |storyboards= |concept= File:Unidentified-Big-Browed-Species-Manzella.jpg|Concept art by Ivan Manzella{{WebCite|url=https://www.krop.com/ivanmanzella|text=Ivan Manzella Creatures & Character Designs|author=Manzella, Ivan|work=[https://www.krop.com Krop]|archivedate=20250715083228}} File:TaibikConcept-ArtofAcolyte.png|Concept art by Ivan Manzella |digital= |in-progress= }} ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Taibik Kajok}} *{{Acolyte|Day (episode)}} {{1st}} *{{Acolyte|Night}} *{{Acolyte|Teach / Corrupt}} ==Sources== *''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' {{1stID|Taibik Kajok}} *''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'' ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |ka=ტაიბიკ კაჯოკი }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Kajok, Taibik}} [[Category:Huwawans]] [[Category:Individuals with he/him pronouns]] [[Category:Males]]
